design.question: Do level-preserving simple residual forecasts help, and is weather hybrid harm in the history-frequency tone plane or elsewhere?
design.baseline_mean: saved future tone + mean(original float64 history minus saved fitted past tone)
design.baseline_last: saved future tone + last(original float64 history minus saved fitted past tone)
design.abstention_baselines: No extracted tone: plain history mean or last observed temperature. No native fallback or method selection.
design.projection: Identical natural_gain_location.partition: QR of sin/cos at saved past-only frequency on32-step future grid; target unchanged, projected errors ONLY diagnostic.
design.abstention_partition: No plane defined; exact identical native/hybrid implies zero gain and zero update, retained in aggregates.
design.aggregation: Every gain and update-energy divided by original window history variance, then average windows within station, then equal8 stations; counts4/4/4/4/4/2/4/4.
design.uncertainty: Reuse primary4096 paired8-station bootstrap draws; descriptive because shared weather induces dependence. No new inferential or significance claim.

natural_comparison.scope: Existing all64 electricity sources per model; natural forecasts/targets already own-history standardized. Compare descriptive partition signs, not a matched causal domain effect.

limits: tones_zero physical zero drops DC; its huge loss is NOT useful evidence for residual necessity.
Future tone-plane projection is not ground-truth component labeling; over32 hours sin/cos can overlap trends or levels.
In-plane update includes both added continuation and changed native residual response; cannot attribute it solely to bad classical continuation.
Native outputs are medians, not means. Chronological observation holdout does not imply unseen locations/distribution.
design.budget: Saved arrays only, CPU1; no downloads, native calls, fits, threshold tuning or forecast selection.

audit.orthogonal_method: Independent B inv(B.T B) B.T versus original QR

interpretation.primary_unchanged: Frozen native-versus-hybrid negative primary and audit are final; all primary completion-manifest files reverified unchanged.
interpretation.tones_zero: The physical-zero-residual control omits temperature DC. Its50.726728059060875 normalized loss is NOT useful evidence for residual necessity, nor does it isolate tone quality.
interpretation.level_controls: Posthoc mean-residual and last-observed-residual controls preserve level. Both have higher observed equal-station loss than native and hybrid; this compares two simple residual rules only, not proof a learned/native residual is necessary.
interpretation.geometry: Both tone-plane and off-plane weather gains are negative. Off-plane accounts for0.8796656098093939 of net Bolt harm and0.5767294780931997 of net TimesFM harm. These ratios use aggregate signed losses; they are not causal fractions.
interpretation.attribution: Most observed harm is outside the fixed tone plane, especially Bolt. Bad continuation alone is not established: the in-plane update includes added tones plus changed native residual response, and finite-horizon sin/cos can overlap level/trend.
interpretation.electricity: TimesFM electricity gain is positive in both plane and off-plane, unlike weather. Bolt electricity total gain is slightly negative, not an electricity-positive result for both models.
interpretation.limits: Posthoc reused observations, descriptive8-station bootstrap with shared-weather dependence, versus64 electricity series. No matched causal domain comparison, confirmation, or training-prior attribution.
